learn.title: Data integration and analysis
objectives: Choose Azure Data Factory, Fabric Data Factory or Databricks for batch data integration, and pick the right integration runtime (Azure, self-hosted, Azure-SSIS)
Decide between ETL and ELT, full and incremental loads, and batch and real-time processing
Choose an analytics engine: Microsoft Fabric (lakehouse, warehouse), Azure Synapse Analytics (dedicated or serverless SQL pools, Spark) or Azure Databricks
Design streaming analytics with Event Hubs as the ingestion source and Azure Stream Analytics, Azure Data Explorer or Databricks for processing
Apply the medallion architecture and cost controls (pause, auto-termination, file formats) in an analytics design
concepts: Azure Data Factory (ADF)

Serverless, managed data integration service. Pipelines group activities (copy, data flow, notebook, stored procedure); linked services hold connection info; datasets describe the data; triggers start pipelines.
Integration runtime (IR)

The compute ADF uses. Azure IR: cloud data movement and mapping data flows (optionally in a managed virtual network). Self-hosted IR: reaches private or on-premises sources with outbound-only connections. Azure-SSIS IR: runs existing SSIS packages.
Mapping data flow
Visual, code-free transformation in ADF that runs on Spark clusters managed by ADF. Runs only on the Azure IR.
Microsoft Fabric
SaaS analytics platform on a single capacity: OneLake storage, Data Factory (pipelines, Dataflow Gen2), lakehouse, warehouse, Real-Time Intelligence and Power BI.
OneLake

One logical data lake per Fabric tenant. Tables are stored in Delta Parquet. Shortcuts point to data in ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3 and other places without copying it; mirroring replicates operational databases into OneLake.
Synapse dedicated SQL pool
Provisioned MPP data warehouse sized in DWUs. Can be paused. Tables are hash-distributed, round-robin or replicated, with clustered columnstore by default.
Synapse serverless SQL pool
No infrastructure to provision; query files in the data lake with T-SQL (OPENROWSET, external tables) and pay for the data processed.
Azure Databricks
Managed Apache Spark platform with Delta Lake, collaborative notebooks, Unity Catalog governance, Auto Loader and Structured Streaming. Good for data engineering and ML.
Azure Stream Analytics
Serverless real-time engine using a SQL-like language with windowing (tumbling, hopping, sliding, session, snapshot), reference data joins and many outputs, including Power BI.
Azure Data Explorer (ADX)
Fast analytics over large volumes of logs and telemetry with KQL. Ingests directly from Event Hubs; retention and hot cache policies control cost.
Medallion architecture
Bronze holds raw data as ingested, silver holds cleansed and conformed data, gold holds aggregated, business-ready data for reporting.
ETL vs ELT
ETL transforms before loading into the target. ELT loads raw data first and transforms it with the target's own scalable compute (lake, Spark or MPP warehouse).
comparisons: Self-hosted IR for on-premises or private-network sources (installed on your machines, outbound 443 only). Azure IR for cloud-to-cloud copy and data flows; use a managed virtual network for private endpoints.
Dedicated: predictable, high-concurrency warehouse workloads with provisioned compute you can pause. Serverless: ad hoc or exploratory queries over lake files, billed per data processed.
Fabric: SaaS, one capacity, minimal admin, integrated Power BI. Synapse: PaaS workspace with SQL pools and Spark. Databricks: Spark-first engineering and ML with Unity Catalog.
Stream Analytics vs Azure Data Explorer
Stream Analytics: continuous queries that compute results as events arrive (alerts, windows). ADX: store and interactively query huge volumes of telemetry with KQL.
Stream Analytics vs Databricks Structured Streaming
Stream Analytics: SQL, serverless, low admin. Databricks: code-heavy streaming in Python/Scala, custom ML scoring and Delta Lake pipelines.
Batch is cheaper and simpler when hours of latency are acceptable. Choose streaming only when the requirement is seconds or minutes.
traps: Mapping data flows cannot run on a self-hosted IR; they need the Azure IR.
A watermark-based incremental load misses deleted rows; use change data capture when deletes must be replicated.
Stream Analytics windows use arrival time unless you use TIMESTAMP BY with the event time field.
A Fabric lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint is read-only; use a Fabric warehouse for T-SQL inserts, updates and multi-table transactions.
A paused dedicated SQL pool still incurs storage charges; only compute billing stops.
Hash-distributing a fact table on a low-cardinality or skewed column causes data skew and slow queries.
revision: On-premises source behind a firewall: self-hosted IR. Existing SSIS packages: Azure-SSIS IR.
Code-free transformation at scale in ADF: mapping data flows. Business-analyst Power Query in Fabric: Dataflow Gen2.
Large fact table: hash distribution on a high-cardinality join column. Small dimension: replicated. Staging: round-robin.
Real-time SQL over Event Hubs with alerts or Power BI output: Stream Analytics.
Interactive KQL over billions of telemetry rows: Azure Data Explorer (or Eventhouse in Fabric).
Use data where it lives in Fabric: OneLake shortcuts. Replicate an operational database without pipelines: Fabric mirroring.
Cut Spark cost: job compute instead of all-purpose clusters, auto-termination, autoscaling.
Cut serverless SQL cost: Parquet or Delta instead of CSV, plus partitioning to reduce data scanned.
